verdict.rationale: Mastra Code lets you decide which integrations the agent gets: MCP servers are set through file-based or programmatic configs, browser tools appear only when a browser provider is set, and custom tools are added explicitly. It also offers a headless approval policy that can deny tool approvals, and directory access outside the project root requires user approval. However, the docs show no per-tool allowlist or denylist and no team-wide policy enforcement, so lead-level access control is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit per-tool or per-integration allow/deny permissions, org or team policy enforcement for an engineering lead, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can control which external tools and integrations the agent is allowed to access

citations.quote: Programmatic MCP server configs, merged with file-based configs
Browser provider; when set the agent gains browser tools
`deny` refuses approvals and aborts on suspension
The user is prompted to approve or deny the request.
